If the universe ends with the big freeze, then what will happen to stars and black holes?
Heat death, complete entropy, total lack of motion: 2009 article on the subject http://www.universetoday.com/36917/big-freeze/

All correct ^.

Eventually, after complete thermal equilibrium (heat death), particles (protons, neutrons, electrons) will decay into energy (photons) (yes, even they have half-lives, but they're on the timescale of billions of years or more).

Now, as the universe increasingly expands, all of those photons will eventually get redshifted to zero energy.

Black holes will eventually evaporate due to hawking radiation.

'The big freeze' basically means the point in time that the last star has burnt out and the last black hole evaporated. Interstellar dust would be sufficiently spread out that it can no longer clump together to form new stars.
